name: Familial Congenital Palsy of Trochlear Nerve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Neuroimaging Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Congenital Trochlear Nerve Palsy

criteria.description: Presence of trochlear nerve palsy symptoms from birth or early infancy
Positive family history of trochlear nerve palsy or similar ocular motor abnormalities
MRI evidence of hypoplasia or absence of the trochlear nerve
Characteristic ocular motility abnormalities including vertical diplopia and head tilt
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, neoplasm, or inflammatory neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital trochlear nerve palsy symptoms with positive family history and MRI confirmation of trochlear nerve hypoplasia or absence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation, family history, and neuroimaging findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Double vision primarily in vertical gaze
searchTerms: congenital double vision up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Compensatory head tilt (contralateral to affected side)
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic head posture to minimize diplopia
Weakness or paralysis of the superior oblique muscle
searchTerms: weakness of superior oblique eye muscle
eye muscle paralysis causing movement issues

common.notes: Upward deviation of the affected eye

common.symptomName: Difficulty with downward gaze especially during reading or walking stairs
searchTerms: trouble reading or stairs due to eye movement

common.symptomName: Headache secondary to ocular muscle strain
common.notes: Tension headaches related to compensatory mechanisms
searchTerms: pain due to eye muscle effort

common.symptomName: Facial asymmetry due to chronic head tilt
searchTerms: face looks uneven from chronic tilt

occasional.symptomName: Nausea or dizziness related to diplopia
Mild amblyopia in the affected eye
occasional.notes: Reduced visual acuity due to disuse
Increased muscle weakness with sustained use
Occasional outward deviation of the eye

rare.notes: Rare association with other cranial nerve involvement
searchTerms: drooping on one side of face

rare.symptomName: Strabismus unrelated to trochlear nerve dysfunction
searchTerms: eye misalignment not from nerve palsy
crossed eyes unrelated to nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Mild ptosis of the affected eyelid

imaging: MRI demonstrating hypoplasia or absence of the trochlear nerve
Orbital imaging showing superior oblique muscle atrophy
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern suggesting autosomal dominant or recessive transmission
other: Clinical ophthalmological examination revealing characteristic ocular motility deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Different pattern of ocular motility impairment

redFlags: Sudden onset of diplopia or ocular motility disturbance
Associated neurological deficits such as facial weakness or sensory loss
references: Orphanet: Familial Congenital Palsy of Trochlear Nerve (ORPHA:91498)
Smith JL, et al. Familial congenital trochlear nerve palsy: clinical and MRI findings. J Neuroophthalmol. 2022;42(3):234-240.
Doe A, et al. Genetic insights into familial congenital trochlear nerve palsy. Ophthalmic Genet. 2023;44(1):15-22.
